LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: The check reaches outside the output file: "...(gang-sheet.pdf) or its delivery manifest states...". An annotator judging gang-sheet.pdf cannot judge a separate manifest, and the check has two possible places to look. The source rule (meridian_sheet_spec.txt: interior negative space 'resolve deliberately ... unless you say so') can be judged from the sheet alone.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Modify H018 to: "“Sticker imposed production sheet” (gang-sheet.pdf) carries a note for each sticker saying whether its interior islands are weeded or left on the sheet." Keep k_id K1_Q3.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: These checks are near-duplicates on the same output. "Kraft #C8A97E and Warm Cream #F3E7D3 are never the main ink" follows from a stronger check already on each file. On the bag SVGs and proofs, H010 says the main ink is solid Roast Brown, Ash Green or Brick Red. On the companions, H006 (SVG) and H005 (proof) say the main ink is Roast Brown, Ash Green or Brick Red. On the window mark, H014, H019 and H020 (SVG) and H014, H018 and H019 (proof) assign an ink to every part. Any file that passes the positive check must also pass the negative one, so these checks score the same fact twice.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Retire each one, with covered_by pointing to the positive main-ink check on the same output: bag SVG and proof H010; companion SVG H006; companion proof H005; window mark SVG H014, H019 and H020; window mark proof H014, H018 and H019. Point the coverage cells for the Kraft and Cream 'never main ink' rule to those ids.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: The opacity check also says each area is a "palette colour". That repeats the palette-hex check on the same proof (window H012, bag H008, companion H003). It makes the opacity check two facts and partly duplicates another check.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Remove the palette clause, for example for the window mark proof: "Apart from anti-aliased edges, every inked area on “Transparent sticker proof - Window mark” (sticker-proof-window-mark.png) is flat and fully opaque, with no tint, gradient or shadow." Apply the same wording to all six proofs.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: Exact type geometry cannot be judged by eye on a PNG proof. H009 asks for an ampersand at exactly 1.6 times the cap height. H008 asks for a "fixed 40 degree curve", which is also jargon a designer cannot measure on pixels. The SVG versions (H010 and H009 on new-sticker-companion-1/2) can be measured, so keep them there.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: On the proofs, change to relative checks. H009: "Any DM Serif Display ampersand on “Transparent sticker proof - Companion 1” (sticker-proof-companion-1.png) is clearly taller than the capitals beside it, never the same height." H008: "Any DM Serif Display MERIDIAN & ASH wordmark on “Transparent sticker proof - Companion 1” (sticker-proof-companion-1.png) is set on a gentle upward arch, not flat." Do the same for Companion 2. For the SVG H009, use plainer wording: "...arches on a curve that spans 40 degrees."

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: "covering no more than 5% of the inked area" is an area measurement nobody can make by eye, least of all on the PNG proofs. There, Ink Black #201914 and Roast Brown #3E2A20 also look almost the same without an eyedropper.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Use an observable form of the same brand rule: "If Ink Black #201914 appears on “…” (file), it is used only for small fine details inside the drawing, never for a main shape, backing shape, type or the wordmark." On the PNG proofs, add "(sample with an eyedropper)" after #201914 if annotators need it.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: This is a compound check. "Every placed sticker has exactly one closed cut path around it on the CutContour layer" and "the layer holds no other paths" are separate facts. The second also overlaps H017 (no cut line drawn into the artwork) and H025 (spot colour).
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Modify H016 to: "On “Sticker imposed production sheet” (gang-sheet.pdf) each of the six placed stickers has exactly one closed cut path around it on the CutContour layer." Add a new K1_Q3 check: "The CutContour layer on “Sticker imposed production sheet” (gang-sheet.pdf) holds no paths other than the six sticker outlines."

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: "Viewed colour managed" is prepress jargon and does not say what the annotator should do. The sheet is CMYK (PSO Coated v3), so an exact sRGB hex match is also not what a person will see.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: "Apart from the CutContour paths, every colour on “Sticker imposed production sheet” (gang-sheet.pdf) is one of the six palette colours: Roast Brown #3E2A20, Kraft #C8A97E, Ash Green #5B6B54, Warm Cream #F3E7D3, Brick Red #A8442E or Ink Black #201914."

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: The check "The MERIDIAN & ASH wordmark is the largest lettering" passes automatically. meridian_window_mark.jpg contains no lettering other than the wordmark, and H011 (SVG) and H009 (proof) forbid adding any. So the check cannot fail and does not measure hierarchy.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Retire both. Set covered_by to H005 and H011 on the SVG, and to H011 and H009 on the proof (arch placement plus no added lettering). LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: "heading or subheading" is unclear on a sticker. In the type scale, step 02 is for counter card and four-pack headers, so a designer will not know what counts as a heading on a 55 mm sticker.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: "If a flat title line other than the MERIDIAN & ASH wordmark appears on “Original companion sticker - Companion 1” (new-sticker-companion-1.svg), it is set in DM Serif Display Regular capitals." Use the same wording on Companion 2 and on both companion proofs.

FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.problem: The brief's companion bullet 'The drawing belongs stylistically beside the recovered collection.' (deliverable_groups new-sticker, and 'subject matter and visual rhythm' in Your design decisions) has no check. It is also missing from the coverage rule list. Coverage D03 ('belongs beside the recovered designs') cites H003, which tests originality, and the new subject check, which tests subject only. Neither tests style or rhythm, so a sticker with the right subject in a clashing style (gradient-free but photoreal, thin-line clip art, and so on) passes every check.
FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.fix: Add one check per companion SVG (K2_Q4 or K1_Q1), for example: 'The drawing on “Original companion sticker - Companion 1” (new-sticker-companion-1.svg) belongs stylistically beside the designs in meridian_bag_moth.jpg, meridian_bag_pourover.jpg and meridian_bag_ridgeline.jpg.' PN1 and PN2 are na via their H001 (proof matches its SVG), and G is na via gang-sheet H011 and H012. Cite the new checks in D03 as well.

FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.problem: The added subject check narrows the brief with invented examples: 'such as coffee, brewing, the roastery or the cafe'. The brief only says 'subject matter ... that fit the coffee collection'. The collection itself includes a moth and a mountain ridge line, and neither fits those examples, so annotators may fail a valid companion such as a bird or an origin landscape.
FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.fix: Reword to: 'The subject of the drawing on “Original companion sticker - Companion 1” (new-sticker-companion-1.svg) fits the Meridian and Ash coffee sticker collection.' Do the same for Companion 2. Or drop the 'such as' list.

FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.problem: Coverage F05 ('Interior negative space remains open at 55 mm') cites the new open-space-clear checks for all six proofs (PW, P1, P2, P3, PN1, PN2). Those checks test that the negative space is transparent, not that interior gaps stay open instead of filling in. A proof whose gaps filled with ink would still pass them. FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.fix: Add one human check per recovered SVG, for example: 'The SVG code of “Recovered sticker artwork - Window mark” (recovered-sticker-window-mark.svg) declares an explicit viewBox.'
